 DOJ says East Potomac Golf Course will close Nov. 15, Trump plans are in the works
 By
 Rex Hoggard , 
 By
 Rex Hoggard 
     Published October 29, 2026 09:17 AM 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email
 Department of Justice attorneys, at the direction of President Donald Trump, pushed back against a U.S. District Court ruling that would halt the redesign and restoration attempts of East Potomac Golf Course , the Washington, D.C., public course that is at the center of a contentious battle between preservationist and the administration.
 On Tuesday, U.S. District Court judge Ana Reyes granted a preliminary injunction to prohibit the Department of Interior from removing any trees from the course. It also requires officials to give a 10-day notice if they plan to close the golf course for any reason other than a federal holiday or a regularly scheduled closure.
 In Wednesday’s response, U.S. Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward wrote that he, “acknowledges the president has twice directed [the Department of] Interior and the National Park Service to close the park by November 15. Accordingly, Interior, acting through counsel, is working to develop a plan to implement that direction and will provide this court with notice [within business 10 days of any unplanned closure of the course],” the response read.
 At the Oct. 19 hearing , Woodward told Reyes, “With regard to the November 15th date … there is no plan to close the course,” despite multiple social media posts from Trump claiming the work on the redesign project would begin on Nov. 15 and last “approximately 15 months.”
 Trump posted on social media that East Potomac is a “debris-ridden wasteland” and a dangerous “national disgrace” along with pictures of the course’s driving and buildings at 10:43 p.m. ET on Wednesday.
 “We will hold the judge, Ana C. Reyes, fully responsible for anybody who is hurt, or killed, on this very dangerous, dilapidated, and unsightly golf course,” Trump wrote.
 “No one will be more thrilled by our plans to renovate the Course and Driving Range than the Local Golfers who have played there for years, and have begged to have their Home Course brought into pristine condition,” he added.
 Government attorneys also filed a notice to appeal Reyes’ preliminary injunction with the D.C. Circuit Appeals Court on Wednesday. A tentative hearing is scheduled for either Friday or Monday.
 A rendition of the Tom Fazio-redesigned course which Trump posted on social media would remove Ohio Drive, which loops around the course, to allow the layout to move closer to the shores of the Potomac River. Ohio Drive is a popular spot for city residents to bike, run and bird watch, according to various reports.
